body:
Large populated games held duplicate map caches and oversized contiguous save buffers. This change shares immutable water/geometry data, compacts bounded counters and Maxima fields, and moves persistence to owned 1 MiB blocks with direct gzip input/output. Header/body loading reuses one validated snapshot; autosave waits for its previous writer before capturing another.

Serialized widths, save/replay/network version gates and simulation scheduling are preserved. Optional level-zero gzip retains its compatibility buffering. Autosave can briefly pause if the previous write has fallen behind; normal play and simulation results are intended to remain identical.

## Validation

Measurements on the original validated macOS arm64 baseline (before rebasing onto current master):

- Late live allocations: 1291 → 1112 MiB. Combined late-game load/save peak: original 4.91 GiB → intermediate 3.96 GiB → final 1.93 GiB (target ≤2.5 GiB).
- Final persistence CPU comparison against the intermediate optimized build: late loading −34.5%, saving −3.2%; all early/mid/late loading, simulation and saving one-sided 95% upper bounds met the 2% regression limit, with seven pairs per fixture.
- Capture versus the previous reserved autosave buffer: CPU −6.8%, wall latency −5.8%.
- 438 selected tests passed. A full 45,000-tick run matched detailed simulation records and exact saved/replay bytes; persistence follow-up matched another 3,072 continuation ticks and saved/replay bytes. Fault tests cover malformed gzip, serialization/allocation/worker exceptions, atomic cleanup and slow autosave backpressure.
- Client/server release builds passed. Linux/Windows execution and an interactive maintainer playtest remain unverified.

Independent review is complete and rechecked. It found two allocation-failure ownership leaks: a block allocated before pointer-table growth, and an inflated backend returned before stream-wrapper allocation. Both are fixed in the follow-up commit. Added comments document snapshot/capture lifetimes, committed-byte and capacity invariants, compact numeric bounds, shared-cache lifetime and canonicalization, and original-header hashing. Broad style normalization and legacy gzip RAII cleanup remain optional follow-ups.

Rebase integration retains new master hardening: 256 MiB compressed input/output limit, a separate 2 GiB expanded limit to accept known ~1 GiB late saves, and Maxima's explicit 16,777,216-entry continuation limit for large geometry. Writers obey reader size limits before atomic replacement. Boundary tests cover exact-limit CRC handling and over-limit rejection. These limits are explicitly different from incoming master's 256 MiB expansion/generic one-million-entry defaults, which rejected valid large fixtures.

Master independently advanced to save version 127 and protocol 50 for sixteen-team support; this PR does not modify those version gates. Pre-rebase exact-byte/CPU evidence therefore belongs to the original validated baseline, not the current-master executable. Final source is rebased onto `master` at `62b1988da`, including security PRs #571 and #576. Client/server release builds and all 474 selected cases passed (420 unit, 54 persistence/security/continuation/compatibility). The late legacy fixture loaded and saved at 1.90 GiB peak; its output matches the prior version127 integration save exactly. It also reloaded successfully in the earlier integration run. Paired CPU benchmarks were not repeated on newer master. Linux/Windows execution and interactive play remain unverified locally. Hosted PR CI is queued; master has no required status-check rule.

[Independent review and resolution notes](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/codex/late-game-memory-evidence/artifacts/memory-optimization/pr-integration/independent-review.md) · [Current-master integration evidence](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/codex/late-game-memory-evidence/artifacts/memory-optimization/pr-integration/integration-review.md). [Validation evidence](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/codex/late-game-memory-evidence/artifacts/memory-optimization/pr-integration) is published on a separate branch, including reports, JUnit, raw timing data, an initial fixture, checksum stream and a final save/replay. The bundle contains hashes for larger local artifacts rather than their multi-gigabyte payloads. Generated artifacts are excluded from this implementation branch.
title: Reduce engine memory and eliminate save/load buffer peaks
